newsitem.title: USA: NYS agency drops LILCO deal from Wed.'s agenda.
newsitem.headline: NYS agency drops LILCO deal from Wed.'s agenda.

text.p: The New York State Assembly, which is probing a proposal for the state to partially take over Long Island Lighting Co, asked a key state agency to drop the item from the agenda for Wednesday, a state official said.

"That has been removed from today's agenda at the request of the state Assembly," said Judith Kenny, who represents the budget director, Patricia Woodworth, at meetings of the New York State Public Authorities Control Board.
The Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, the Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, and Gov George Pataki, serve on the agency's three-member board, which means they each have a veto.

A spokesman for the Speaker, who has raised a number of concerns about the proposed deal, said more time was needed to gather information, adding the Assembly asked the Authority to postpone its vote until June 18.

"We had not finished our hearings and the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) hadn't either, so we asked that it be postponned until the next regularly scheduled Public Authorities Control Board meeting," said Charles Carrier.

Pataki in mid-March proposed that LIPA, which was created in 1986 to acquire the Long Island Lighting Co, buy assets from LILCO and Brooklyn Union Gas, which plan to merge. The deal would be financed by the sale of $7.3 billion of tax-exempt bonds, the nation's largest-ever such offering.
A LILCO spokeswoman said that it joined Brooklyn Union and LIPA and sent the state agency what she called an unsigned, definitive agreement for it to review.
"And we're hopeful the Public Authorities Control Board will take up the matter as soon as possible," she said.
W.J. Catacosinos, chairman and chief executive of LILCO, in prepared remarks, warned the Assembly at a hearing that delays could jeopardize the deal.
